name: Non-acquired Pituitary Hormone Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hypopituitarism

criteria.description: Documented deficiency of one or more anterior pituitary hormones confirmed by biochemical testing
MRI evidence of pituitary hypoplasia, aplasia, or stalk interruption
Presence of clinical signs consistent with hormone deficiencies such as growth failure, hypoglycemia, or micropenis in males
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with pituitary development (e.g., PROP1, POU1F1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of documented pituitary hormone deficiency confirmed biochemically plus supportive pituitary imaging abnormalities and consistent clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe neonatal hypoglycemia due to cortisol deficiency
searchTerms: severe low blood sugar in newborns

pathognomonic.symptomName: Micropenis or cryptorchidism in affected male infants
Growth failure with markedly delayed bone age
searchTerms: poor growth with delayed bone development
slow growth and late bone age
pale or yellow skin in newborns
jaundice and pale complexion in infants

common.symptomName: Fatigue and lethargy related to hypothyroidism
searchTerms: tiredness and sleepiness from low thyroid
lethargy due to thyroid hormone deficiency
low blood pressure from adrenal insufficiency

common.symptomName: Delayed puberty or absent secondary sexual characteristics
searchTerms: no development of secondary sexual features

common.symptomName: Cold intolerance due to central hypothyroidism
searchTerms: sensitivity to cold from low thyroid hormone

occasional.symptomName: Headache related to pituitary hypoplasia or cystic lesions
searchTerms: pain in head related to pituitary cysts

occasional.symptomName: Visual field defects from pituitary stalk abnormalities
searchTerms: loss of side vision from pituitary stalk issues
visual field loss due to pituitary problems
blind spots caused by pituitary abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: Hyponatremia due to inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
searchTerms: low blood sodium from excess antidiuretic hormone
low sodium caused by inappropriate ADH secretion
seizures caused by low blood sugar in infants

rare.symptomName: Craniofacial abnormalities such as midline defects
searchTerms: unusual skull or facial bone shape
craniofacial malformations affecting center of face
seizures not caused by low sugar
epileptic episodes unrelated to glucose levels

laboratory: Low serum levels of pituitary-dependent hormones (GH, ACTH, TSH, LH, FSH, prolactin)
Low target gland hormones (cortisol, free T4, sex steroids, IGF-1)
Hypoglycemia with low cortisol and growth hormone during stress
imaging: MRI showing pituitary hypoplasia, absent or thin pituitary stalk, or ectopic posterior pituitary bright spot
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as PROP1, POU1F1, HESX1, LHX3, LHX4
other: Abnormal stimulation tests confirming hormone deficiencies

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, tumor, infection, or radiation
Imaging showing mass lesion or pituitary damage
Deficiency limited to growth hormone only

redFlags: Severe neonatal hypoglycemia unresponsive to glucose infusion
Failure to thrive with multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies
Sudden onset adrenal crisis or coma
references: Pitteloud N, et al. Congenital Hypopituitarism: Diagnosis and Management. Endocr Rev. 2020.
